title: What If the Sun Vanished Right Now? ☀️
description:
The Sun disappears. For 8 minutes, you wouldn't even know.
Its last light and its gravity are still on the way. Then the lights go out, Earth sails off in a straight line, and the surface freezes. But under the ice, and deep underground, something keeps going.

What should we make disappear next? Tell us in the comments.

#shorts #space #science #sun #whatif
facts_checked: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth -> https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/all-about-the-sun/en/ ; https://www.universetoday.com/articles/how-long-does-it-take-sunlight-to-reach-the-earth

Changes in gravity travel at the speed of light, so Earth keeps orbiting for ~8 min, then moves off in a straight line -> https://www.scienceabc.com/nature/universe/what-happen-sun-suddenly-disappeared-earth-life-light-night-dark-moon.html ; https://www.businessinsider.in/heres-what-would-happen-if-the-sun-disappeared-right-now/articleshow/48430503.cms ; https://physicsworld.com/a/spectacular-collision-of-two-neutron-stars-observed-for-first-time/

The Moon shines with reflected sunlight, so it would go dark too -> https://www.scienceabc.com/nature/universe/what-happen-sun-suddenly-disappeared-earth-life-light-night-dark-moon.html ; https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/all-about-the-sun/en/

Within about a week the surface drops below freezing -> https://experts.caltech.edu/news/caltech-question-month-if-sun-ceased-exist-right-now-how-long-would-mankind-survive-would ; https://www.popsci.com/science/article/2013-07/if-sun-went-out-how-long-could-life-earth-survive/ ; Business Insider (32F after a week)

After a year colder than about -73 C (Caltech: below 200 K; PopSci: -100 F; Business Insider: -150 F) -> https://experts.caltech.edu/news/caltech-question-month-if-sun-ceased-exist-right-now-how-long-would-mankind-survive-would ; https://www.popsci.com/science/article/2013-07/if-sun-went-out-how-long-could-life-earth-survive/

Oceans freeze over on top; ice insulates and deep water stays liquid a long time (Caltech: ~1,000 years for the deepest water; PopSci: hundreds of thousands of years) -> 'for centuries' is consistent with both

Microbes deep underground / in the crust could survive -> https://experts.caltech.edu/news/caltech-question-month-if-sun-ceased-exist-right-now-how-long-would-mankind-survive-would ; https://www.popsci.com/science/article/2013-07/if-sun-went-out-how-long-could-life-earth-survive/
The Sun has about 5 billion years left -> https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/sun-age/en/ ; https://science.gsfc.nasa.gov/attic/cosmicopia.gsfc.nasa.gov/qa_sun.html
